diagnostic_evidence.quote: These results are consistent with those established in \cite{HL2020} and \cite{HJL2021}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the examples "demonstrate the sharpness of the convergence rates", i.e. that the obtained rates are optimal. The paper's formal content consists exclusively of upper bounds: Theorem main theorem ex1 gives |u-u_h| <= C h^{Gamma(alpha,delta,q0)} and Theorem main theorem ex1 CLT the analogous bound for the limit theorem; Section 4 only computes these rates and notes that special cases match the (upper-bound) rates of prior work. No lower bound, optimality argument, or sharpness analysis appears anywhere, so sharpness is not established.

failure_location.quote: Concrete examples are provided to illustrate our results and demonstrate the sharpness of the convergence rates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Soften/delete the phrase (e.g. "illustrate our results") or add an actual lower-bound/optimality analysis.
issues.overall_effect: Readers are misled about the strength of the rate guarantees; no formal result is affected.
issues.title: Prose overclaim: examples do not demonstrate sharpness of the convergence rates
issues.why_classification: Purely expository overclaim; correcting it changes no formal statement, rate, or guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\zeta \in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{d})$ be a nonnegative mollifier with unit integral and compact support in $[-1,0] \times B_{1}$. For any bounded function $v : [0,1] \times \mathbb{R}^{3d} \to \mathbb{R}$
for all \( \varepsilon \in (0,1) \), \( h \in (0,1) \), and \( (t,x,y,z) \in [h,1] \times \mathbb{R}^{3d} \), where \( u^{\varepsilon} := u \ast \zeta_{\varepsilon} \).

issues.failure_explanation: Since ζ is supported in τ ∈ [-1,0], the rescaled kernel ζ_ε is supported in τ ∈ [-ε²,0], so v^ε(t,x,y,z) averages v(t-τ,·) over t-τ ∈ [t,t+ε²]. For t ∈ (1-ε²,1] this requires values of v at times > 1, but v (in particular u and u_h) is defined only on [0,1]×R^{3d}. Hence u^ε and u_h^ε are undefined on part of the region [h,1]×R^{3d} on which (C2), (C3) and the proof of Theorem main theorem invoke them (the comparison argument needs S(h,x,y,z,u^ε(t,...),u^ε(t-h,...)) ≥ -E₂(ε,h) for all (t,x,y,z) ∈ [h,1]×R^{3d}).

failure_location.quote: v^{\varepsilon}(t,x,y,z) := (v \ast \zeta_{\varepsilon})(t,x,y,z) := \int_{-\varepsilon^{2}}^{0} \int_{|e| < \varepsilon} v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e) \, de \, d\tau

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Extend u and u_h beyond t = 1 in a regularity-preserving way (e.g. u(t) := Ễ[φ(x+ξ_t,y+η_t,z+ζ_t)] and u_h(t) := Ê[u_h(t-h,·)] for t ∈ (1,1+ε²]); the bounds (u_regularity) and (uh_regularity) extend and all arguments then go through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The subsolution/supersolution properties (C2), (C3) and the derivation of the error bounds E₁, E₂ are incomplete as written for t ∈ (1-ε²,1]; the proofs of the main error-bound and rate theorems, which rely on them, are incomplete as written (their statements are unaffected once the gap is patched).
issues.title: Krylov mollification v^ε is undefined near t = 1 but is used there
issues.why_classification: Routine standard extension; no statement, rate, or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: u_h is piecewise constant in t on the grid cells [kh,(k+1)h), with jumps |u_h(kh)-u_h((k-1)h)| of order C_φ((M²_{X₁})^{1/2}+M¹_{Y₁}+M_Z)h^{1/2} at grid points — exactly why Lemma uh_regularity (ii) contains the additive h^{1/2} term. The paper drops this floor twice. (a) Property (C1) asserts a uniform 1/2-Hölder bound in t with no h^{1/2} term, which is false: taking t,t' on opposite sides of a grid point with |t-t'| → 0 gives |u_h(t)-u_h(t')| → |jump| ~ h^{1/2} > 0 while C₀|t-t'|^{1/2} → 0. (b) The bound ‖u_h - u_h^ε‖_∞ ≤ 2C₀ε is false: the mollification window [t,t+ε²] crosses grid points, so ‖u_h-u_h^ε‖ is of order C₀(ε+h^{1/2}) and, for generic data, is bounded below by c·h^{1/2} for every ε > 0 (it does not vanish as ε → 0). The lower-bound part of the proof of Theorem main theorem uses this false step (u-u_h ≤ 2C₀h^{1/2}+2C₀ε+‖u_h-u_h^ε‖+E₁), so the stated constants 2C₀h^{1/2} and 4C₀ε in Theorem main theorem (i) (and in the lower bound of Theorem main theorem CLT) are unsupported as written; the correct chain yields (2C₀+C)h^{1/2}+min((4C₀+C)ε+E₁).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reinstate the h^{1/2} floor: state (C1) with (|t-t'|^{1/2}+h^{1/2}) as in Lemma uh_regularity (ii), and replace ‖u_h-u_h^ε‖ ≤ 2C₀ε by ≤ C₀(ε+h^{1/2}); the proof of Theorem main theorem (i) then yields u-u_h ≤ (2C₀+C)h^{1/2}+min((4C₀+C)ε+E₁), a pure constant adjustment with the same structure.
issues.overall_effect: Property (C1) as stated is false; the mollification estimate (uh_mollifer) is false; the explicit constants in the lower bounds of Theorem main theorem and Theorem main theorem CLT are unsupported. The bound structure (h^{1/2} term plus ε/E₁ balancing) and all convergence rates survive with adjusted constants.
issues.title: Dropped h^{1/2} floor in u_h's time regularity: false (C1) property, false mollification bound, unsupported constants in Theorem main theorem (i)
issues.why_classification: Local repair supplied by the paper's own Lemma uh_regularity (ii); no new argument is needed and the bound structure, all rates, and all downstream guarantees survive with enlarged constants.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Using H\"older's inequality with $p_1 = 3$, $q_1 = \frac{3}{2}$, and $p_2 = q_2 = 2$, it follows that
This yields the lower bound for $\delta$, given by $\delta > \alpha \frac{q_1}{2} \geq \frac{3}{4}\alpha$.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed estimate rests on the pointwise interpolation |Δ|^{q₁} ≤ (2‖D_xω‖)^{q₁-δ}(‖D_{xz}²ω‖h^{1/α}|Z|)^δ, which is valid only for δ ≤ q₁; with p₁ = 3 the conjugate is q₁ = 3/2, so for δ > 3/2 the exponent q₁-δ is negative and the interpolation fails (whenever the Lipschitz bound ‖D_{xz}²ω‖h^{1/α}|Z| is the active one). Assumption (v) admits δ ∈ (3/2,α) whenever α ∈ (3/2,2), and in that regime the lemma's stated bound — which then contains ‖D_xω‖^{(3-2δ)/3} with negative exponent — is false. Counterexample: on a linear expectation space take Z symmetric α-stable, X = √Q₀·sign(Z), Y ≡ 0, Θ = {(F₀,0,Q₀)} (Assumption 2 then holds for every δ ∈ (3/2,α)); for ω = a^{3/2}sin(a^{-1/2}x)sin(Bz/a) (so ‖D_xω‖ = a, ‖D_{xz}²ω‖ = B, ‖D_x³ω‖ = 1) the true error R contains an unmatched X-Z cross term √Q₀E|Z|B h^{1/α-1/2} (from Ê[sign(Z)sin((B/a)h^{1/α}|Z|)] ≈ (B/a)h^{1/α}E|Z|), i.e. R ≳ cB h^{(2-α)/(2α)}, while the claimed δ-term 2M₀h^{(4δ-3α)/(6α)}a^{(3-2δ)/3}B^{2δ/3} → 0 as a → ∞ and all other claimed terms are O(h^{1/2})+o(1); since (2-α)/(2α) < 1/2 < (4δ-3α)/(6α) for δ > 3/2, the stated bound is violated. Remark remark_delta justifies the δ-range only from below (δ > αq₁/2) and omits the binding constraint δ ≤ q₁ = 3/2.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Assumption (v) to δ ∈ ((3/4)α∨1, min(α,3/2)] (equivalently replace δ by δ' = min(δ,3/2) throughout, noting M^{δ'}_{Z₁} ≤ (M^δ_{Z₁})^{δ'/δ}); all proofs then apply verbatim, but for α ∈ (3/2,2) the provable rate becomes Γ(α,δ',q₀), whose first term is (2-α)/(4α) instead of up to 1/(4α+6).
issues.overall_effect: For α ∈ (3/2,2) with δ ∈ (3/2,α) (admitted by Assumption (v)): Lemma consistency's stated bound is false; the explicit error functions E₁, E₂ in the proof of Theorem main theorem, and hence the error bounds of Theorems main theorem and main theorem CLT instantiated with them, are false/unestablished in that regime; the convergence rates Γ(α,δ,q₀) claimed in Theorems main theorem ex1 and main theorem ex1 CLT are unsupported there, as is the optimization sup over δ ∈ ((3/4)α∨1,α) of (4δ-3α)/(2α(2δ+3)) = 1/(4α+6) used in the proof. For α ∈ (1,3/2] (or δ ≤ 3/2) nothing is affected.
issues.title: Invalid Hölder interpolation for δ > 3/2: Lemma consistency false and advertised rates unsupported for α ∈ (3/2,2)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a local hypothesis-range restriction needing no new proof architecture and excluding no distributions (finite δ-moment with δ > 3/2 implies finite 3/2-moment); however, for α ∈ (3/2,2) the guaranteed convergence rate is weakened by a constant factor (the first term of Γ drops from up to 1/(4α+6) to (2-α)/(4α)) — a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Combining \eqref{2.4}, \eqref{2.7}, and Assumption \ref{assump2}, we complete the proof.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes R₁₁ ≤ ½h‖∂_t²ω‖ with a moment-independent constant ½ (all other terms carry moment factors dominated by 2M₀), but the stated bound controls the h‖∂_t²ω‖ term only by 2M₀h‖∂_t²ω‖. Assumption 2 does not imply M₀ ≥ ¼: all seven summands of M₀ can be made arbitrarily small, e.g. X₁ ≡ 0 and Y₁ ≡ 0 (degenerate drift and diffusion, explicitly in scope) together with Z₁ having α-stable tails of arbitrarily small mass Λ̲ > 0 — a setting satisfying (i)-(vi). For such data and any spatially constant ω = f(t) ∈ C_b^∞, one has G = 0, \hat l_ω = 0 and R = |f'(t) - (f(t)-f(t-h))/h| ≈ (h/2)‖f''‖, which exceeds the claimed 2M₀h‖f''‖ whenever M₀ < ¼. Hence the lemma's stated inequality, and the explicit E₁, E₂ (prefactor 4C₀K_ζM₀) derived from it, are false as written in the small-moment regime.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the prefactor 2M₀ in Lemma consistency (and 4C₀K_ζM₀ in (E1), (E2)) by 2M₀+1, or carry the ½h‖∂_t²ω‖ term separately; nothing else changes.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit consistency-error functions E₁(ε,h), E₂(ε,h) in the proof of Theorem main theorem, and hence the explicit error bounds in Theorem main theorem and Theorem main theorem CLT, are not established as stated when M₀ < ¼; all convergence rates are unaffected (constants only).
issues.title: Prefactor 2M₀ in Lemma consistency fails when the moments are small
issues.why_classification: Purely local constant repair; every statement, rate, and guarantee survives with adjusted constants.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let \( \mathcal{L} \subset \mathcal{L}_0 \) be a non-empty compact convex set.
We take the uncertain set given in \eqref{functionG} as $\Theta=\mathcal{L}\times\Gamma\times\Sigma$.

issues.failure_explanation: The standing framework (Section 2.2) requires L to be a non-empty compact convex subset of L₀ = {F_μ : μ(S) ∈ (Λ̲,Λ̄)}. In the example μ = k₁δ_{-1} + k₂δ_{+1}, so μ(S) = k₁+k₂, and the index set is defined as Λ = (Λ̲,Λ̄)². For k ∈ (Λ̲,Λ̄)² one gets μ(S) = k₁+k₂ ∈ (2Λ̲,2Λ̄), which is not contained in (Λ̲,Λ̄) (e.g. k₁,k₂ near Λ̄ give μ(S) near 2Λ̄ > Λ̄), so the corresponding F_μ lie outside L₀ and the example's L is not a subset of L₀; moreover (Λ̲,Λ̄)² is open, so L is not compact. Hence the example's uncertainty set Θ = L×Γ×Σ violates the hypotheses under which the universal robust limit theorem and Assumption 2 are posed, and the subsequent verification that {(X_i,Y_i,Z_i)} satisfies Assumption 2 is carried out for an inadmissible L.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine Λ as a compact convex set of k's with k₁+k₂ ∈ (Λ̲,Λ̄) (introducing fresh symbols for the component bounds if desired); all verifications then apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The Section 4 example's construction (and thereby the formal admissibility of the setting used to illustrate Theorems main theorem ex1 and main theorem ex1 CLT) is inconsistent with the framework; all estimates and rates are unaffected once the index set is corrected.
issues.title: Example's Lévy-measure index set Λ = (Λ̲,Λ̄)² is inconsistent with the framework's requirement L ⊂ L₀ compact
issues.why_classification: Routine redefinition of an index set; no argument, rate, or guarantee is affected.
